rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Evil and piety are innate latent dispositions; revelation and outside influences awaken, strengthen, and direct them rather than creating them. The Qur'an also describes this as guidance along the two paths.
rows.anchor: والرسالات والتوجيهات والعوامل الخارجية إنما توقظ هذه الاستعدادات وتشحذها وتوجهها هنا أو هناك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alongside innate dispositions, each person has a conscious, discerning, directing faculty; that faculty bears responsibility.
rows.anchor: إلى جانب هذه الاستعدادات الفطرية الكامنة قوة واعية مدركة موجهة في ذات الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person flourishes by using this faculty to purify the self, develop its capacity for good, and make good prevail over evil.
rows.anchor: فمن استخدم هذه القوة في تزكية نفسه وتطهيرها وتنمية استعداد الخير فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Suppressing and weakening the conscious faculty leads to failure.
rows.anchor: ومن أظلم هذه القوة وخبأها وأضعفها فقد خاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human freedom entails accountability, capacity entails obligation, and divine gift entails duty; choice directs innate capacities toward either good or evil.
rows.anchor: فهي حرية تقابلها تبعة ، وقدرة يقابلها تكليف ، ومنحة يقابلها واجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In mercy, God does not leave people to instinct or unaided will: revelation supplies firm measures, faith-inspiring signs, and guidance in the self and the world, clearing away caprice.
rows.anchor: فأعانه بالرسالات التي تضع له الموازين الثابتة الدقيقة ، وتكشف له عن موحيات الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the conscious faculty sees the path clearly, it chooses knowingly; whatever occurs within this divinely granted freedom fulfills God's encompassing will and decree.
rows.anchor: فتتصرف القوة الواعية حينئذ عن بصيرة وإدراك لحقيقة الاتجاه الذي تختاره وتسير فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This view honors humans by making them capable of choice and responsible for its direction, while locating that freedom within God's will.
rows.anchor: فالحرية والتبعة يضعان هذا الكائن في مكان كريم ، ويقرران له في هذا الوجود منزلة عالية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People bear responsibility for their fate; God's decree concerning them is realized through their own conduct, which should awaken vigilance and reverent caution.
rows.anchor: وهو يعلم أن قدر الله فيه يتحقق من خلال تصرفه هو بنفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People continually need God's stable measures to test whether desire has deceived them, and to stay near God through His guidance and light.
rows.anchor: تشعر هذا الإنسان بالحاجة الدائمة للرجوع إلى الموازين الإلهية الثابتة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Purification has no endpoint: the person can keep cleansing the self in God's abundant light and the flowing springs of existence.
rows.anchor: فلا نهاية لما يملك هذا الإنسان أن يصل إليه من تزكية النفس وتطهيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thamud exemplifies failure: tyranny hid the people from guidance and defiled them, bringing divine anger and destruction; Qutb directs readers to fuller earlier accounts, especially Sura al-Fajr.
rows.anchor: وقد وردت قصة ثمود ونبيها صالح - عليه السلام - في مواضع شتى من القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here Qutb says Thamud denied its prophet because of its transgression; tyranny itself was the cause of denial.
rows.anchor: فكان الطغيان وحده هو سبب التكذيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tyranny appeared in the rise of Thamud's most wretched man, who hamstrung the she-camel and became most wretched through his sin.
rows.anchor: وهو الذي عقر الناقة . وهو أشدها شقاء وأكثرها تعاسة بما ارتكب من الإثم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before the attack, Salih warned them not to touch God's she-camel or the water assigned to it.
rows.anchor: احذروا أن تمسوا ناقة الله أو أن تمسوا الماء الذي جعل لها يوما ولهم يوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The camel was made a sign after they requested a miracle; its special nature is left unspecified because God disclosed no details.
rows.anchor: فجعل الله هذه الناقة آية - ولا بد أنه كان لها شأن خاص لا نخوض في تفصيلاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though one man hamstrung the camel, the whole people shared responsibility because they approved his act and did not stop him; this is a central Islamic principle of shared social accountability.
rows.anchor: ولكنهم جميعا حملوا التبعة وعدوا أنهم عقروها ، لأنهم لم يضربوا على يده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Collective responsibility in this life does not erase individual responsibility for the afterlife; neglecting mutual counsel, urging good, and restraining wrongdoing is itself culpable.
rows.anchor: لا يتعارض مع التبعة الفردية في الجزاء الأخروي حيث لا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Damdam means divine wrath and the punishment following it; the word's sound evokes and pictures a terrifying scene.
rows.anchor: واللفظ ذاته . . ( دمدم )يوحي بما وراءه ، ويصور معناه بجرسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God devastated the land, leveling its upper and lower parts in a scene of violent destruction.
rows.anchor: وقد سوى الله أرضهم عاليها بسافلها ، وهو المشهد الذي يرتسم بعد الدمار العنيف الشديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrasing implies that one who fears no consequences reaches the utmost severity in punishment; it conveys the dread and force of God's punishment.
rows.anchor: فالذي لا يخاف عاقبة ما يفعل ، يبلغ غاية البطش حين يبطش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human nature and cosmic realities are joined by God's measured practice of seizing deniers and tyrants: every matter has its term, appointed time, end, and wisdom.
rows.anchor: سنة الله في أخذ المكذبين والطغاة ، في حدود التقدير الحكيم الذي يجعل لكل شيء أجلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Male and female begin from comparable reproductive material, yet coordinated factors produce each sex and sustain reproduction; discovering those factors does not explain their ordered fit, so chance cannot account for it.
rows.anchor: فلا يبقى إلا أن هنالك مدبرا يخلق الذكر والأنثى لحكمة مرسومة وغاية معلومة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Male and female are a universal created pattern across living species, including plants; only the Creator is singular and unlike anything else.
rows.anchor: والذكر والأنثى شاملان بعد ذلك للأنواع كلها غير الثدييات . فهي مطردة في سائر الأحياء ومنها النبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These cosmic and human signs form the frame for the sura's central truth about deeds and recompense in this life and the next.
rows.anchor: يجعلها السياق القرآني إطارا لحقيقة العمل والجزاء في الحياة الدنيا وفي الحياة الأخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As a gracious act, God undertook to make guidance clear to human nature and awareness through messengers, revelations, and signs, leaving no one an excuse and wronging no one.
rows.anchor: لقد كتب الله على نفسه - فضلا منه بعباده ورحمة - أن يبين الهدى لفطرة الناس ووعيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's ownership encompasses both the afterlife and this first life, leaving those who seek to flee Him nowhere to take refuge.
rows.anchor: فلا يجدون من دونها موئلا : ( وإن لنا للآخرة والأولى )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because God clarified guidance and owns both abodes of action and recompense, He warns people of the blazing fire.
rows.anchor: تفريعا على أن الله كتب على نفسه بيان الهدى للعباد ، وأن له الآخرة والأولى داري الجزاء والعمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only the most wretched of all servants undergoes the blazing fire; Qutb underscores that no greater misery is imaginable.
rows.anchor: أشقى العباد جميعا . وهل بعد الصلي في النار شقوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The most wretched person is one who denies the call and turns away from guidance and the Lord's invitation to seek His promised guidance.
rows.anchor: كذب بالدعوة وتولى عنها . تولى عن الهدى وعن دعوة ربه له ليهديه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The God-fearing giver gives wealth to purify himself, not to repay anyone for a favor; his sole motive is seeking his Lord's highest countenance.
rows.anchor: وما لأحد عنده من نعمة تجزى . إلا ابتغاء وجه ربه الأعلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qutb builds suspense by asking what this purified, sincere giver awaits, calling the Qur'an's announced reward astonishing, unexpected, and unlike the familiar.
rows.anchor: إن الجزاء الذي يطالع القرآن به الأرواح المؤمنة هنا عجيب . ومفاجئ . وعلى غير المألوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The God-fearing giver gives wealth to purify himself, not to repay anyone for a favor; his sole motive is seeking his Lord's highest countenance.
rows.anchor: وما لأحد عنده من نعمة تجزى . إلا ابتغاء وجه ربه الأعلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qutb builds suspense by asking what this purified, sincere giver awaits, calling the Qur'an's announced reward astonishing, unexpected, and unlike the familiar.
rows.anchor: إن الجزاء الذي يطالع القرآن به الأرواح المؤمنة هنا عجيب . ومفاجئ . وعلى غير المألوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reward is contentment permeating the God-fearing giver's heart, soul, limbs, and whole life.
rows.anchor: إنه الرضى ينسكب في قلب هذا الأتقى . إنه الرضى يغمر روحه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This contentment embraces religion, God, decree, and one's share, whether ease or hardship, wealth or poverty; it brings calm and patience rather than anxiety, impatience, or a sense of burden.
rows.anchor: يرضى بدينه . ويرضى بربه . ويرضى بقدره . ويرضى بنصيبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is a reward greater than every other reward, given by God to hearts sincere toward Him; it follows the giver's sacrifice and pursuit of God's face.
rows.anchor: إنه جزاء لا يمنحه إلا الله . وهو يسكبه في القلوب التي تخلص له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's stream of favor never dries up: the Prophet will receive better goodness from God in the hereafter than in worldly life, for God is goodness in both.
rows.anchor: فإن لك عنده في الآخرة من الحسنى خيرا مما يعطيك منها في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God reserves what will satisfy the Prophet: success in his mission, removal of obstacles, victory of his way, and the emergence of truth—his concerns amid opposition, denial, harm, plotting, and mockery.
rows.anchor: من التوفيق في دعوتك ، وإزاحة العقبات من طريقك ، وغلبة منهجك ، وظهور حقك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sura recalls God's care, affection, and gifts from the Prophet's earliest days so he can relive divine mercy, intimacy, and tenderness.
rows.anchor: ليستحضر في خاطره جميل صنع ربه به ، ومودته له ، وفيضه عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God took the Prophet in as an orphan, drawing hearts to care for him, including his uncle Abu Talib despite Abu Talib not sharing his religion.
rows.anchor: وعطف عليك القلوب حتى قلب عمك أبي طالب وهو على غير دينك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made the Prophet inwardly rich through contentment and materially sufficient through his earnings and the wealth of his household, Khadija, so he neither felt poor nor coveted others' wealth.
rows.anchor: كما أغناك بكسبك ومال أهل بيتك [ خديجة رضي الله عنها ] عن أن تحس الفقر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Raised amid confused pagan beliefs and practices, the Prophet found no reassuring way in paganism or among followers of Moses and Jesus who had altered their faith; God guided him through revelation and its way.
rows.anchor: ثم هداك الله بالأمر الذي أوحي به إليك ، وبالمنهج الذي يصلك به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance from doctrinal confusion is the greatest favor, bringing incomparable rest and calm; the verse reassured the Prophet during interrupted revelation, pagan gloating, and the loneliness of separation from his beloved Lord.
rows.anchor: والهداية من حيرة العقيدة وضلال الشعاب فيها هي المنة الكبرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made the Prophet inwardly rich through contentment and materially sufficient through his earnings and the wealth of his household, Khadija, so he neither felt poor nor coveted others' wealth.
rows.anchor: كما أغناك بكسبك ومال أهل بيتك [ خديجة رضي الله عنها ] عن أن تحس الفقر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Raised amid confused pagan beliefs and practices, the Prophet found no reassuring way in paganism or among followers of Moses and Jesus who had altered their faith; God guided him through revelation and its way.
rows.anchor: ثم هداك الله بالأمر الذي أوحي به إليك ، وبالمنهج الذي يصلك به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance from doctrinal confusion is the greatest favor, bringing incomparable rest and calm; the verse reassured the Prophet during interrupted revelation, pagan gloating, and the loneliness of separation from his beloved Lord.
rows.anchor: والهداية من حيرة العقيدة وضلال الشعاب فيها هي المنة الكبرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembering God's care for the Prophet as an orphan prompts him to guide Muslims to care for every orphan, meet every requester's needs, and speak of God's great gift, especially guidance to Islam.
rows.anchor: يوجهه ويوجه المسلمين من ورائه إلى رعاية كل يتيم ، وإلى كفاية كل سائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Honoring the orphan means forbidding oppression, hurt feelings, humiliation, and the breaking of the orphan's spirit.
rows.anchor: إلى إكرام اليتيم والنهي عن قهره وكسر خاطره وإذلاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The needy should be provided for gently and with dignity; Islam replaced a harsh society's disregard for the weak with justice, piety, and respect for God's limits.
rows.anchor: وإلى إغناء السائل مع الرفق به والكرامة ، كانت - كما ذكرنا مرارا - من أهم إيحاءات الواقع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God guards the rights of vulnerable people who lack the strength or weapons to defend them, and is angered by attacks on those rights.
rows.anchor: الذي يحرس حدوده ويغار عليها ويغضب للاعتداء على حقوق عباده الضعفاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Speaking of God's gifts, especially guidance and faith, is a form of gratitude; virtuous service to God's servants completes that thanks as its practical, quiet, beneficial expression.
rows.anchor: فهو صورة من صور الشكر للمنعم . يكملها البر بعباده ، وهو المظهر العملي للشكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sura al-Sharh is Meccan, has eight verses, and followed Sura al-Duha as though completing it, with tenderness, reminders of care, and glad tidings of relief.
rows.anchor: سورة الشرح مكية وآياتها ثمان نزلت هذه السورة بعد سورة الضحى . وكأنها تكملة لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sura suggests the Prophet was burdened by the mission's worries, difficult obstacles, and surrounding plots, and needed support, provision, and strength.
rows.anchor: كان مثقلا بهموم هذه الدعوة الثقيلة ، وأنه كان يحس العبء فادحا على كاهله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening question means God opened the Prophet's heart to the mission, made its path beloved and clear, and gave him joy, rest, ease, and contentment alongside hardship and deprivation.
rows.anchor: ونيسر لك أمرها ? . ونجعلها حبيبة لقلبك ، ونشرع لك طريقها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The burden had weighed on the Prophet's back almost to breaking; God removed it by opening his heart, making the task lighter and easier.
rows.anchor: عبئك الذي أثقل ظهرك حتى كاد يحطمه من ثقله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God eased the burden by enabling the mission, opening hearts to it, and sending revelation that disclosed truth and helped convey it gently to people.
rows.anchor: وبتوفيقك وتيسيرك للدعوة ومداخل القلوب . وبالوحي الذي يكشف لك عن الحقيقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The burden had weighed on the Prophet's back almost to breaking; God removed it by opening his heart, making the task lighter and easier.
rows.anchor: عبئك الذي أثقل ظهرك حتى كاد يحطمه من ثقله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God eased the burden by enabling the mission, opening hearts to it, and sending revelation that disclosed truth and helped convey it gently to people.
rows.anchor: وبتوفيقك وتيسيرك للدعوة ومداخل القلوب . وبالوحي الذي يكشف لك عن الحقيقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God raised Muhammad's name in heaven, on earth, and throughout existence, uniquely joining it with God's name in the testimony of faith; no higher rank follows this.
rows.anchor: رفعناه فجعلنا اسمك مقرونا باسم الله كلما تحركت به الشفاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Across generations, millions invoke Muhammad's noble name with blessings, salutation, and deep love; even being chosen for the divine method elevated him beyond all others.
rows.anchor: حين قدر الله أن تمر القرون ، وتكر الأجيال ، وملايين الشفاه في كل مكان تهتف بهذا الأسم الكريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the Prophet finishes work among people and worldly concerns, he should turn all his effort toward worship, detachment, aspiration, and devotion to God.
rows.anchor: إذا فرغت من هذا كله فتوجه بقلبك كله إذن إلى ما يستحق أن تنصب فيه وتكد وتجهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet should seek God alone, free even from concern for the people he serves through his mission; God is the provision and equipment for the hard road and struggle.
rows.anchor: إلى ربك وحده خاليا من كل شيء حتى من أمر الناس الذين تشتغل بدعوتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sura closes like al-Duha with both tenderness toward the Prophet's burdens and awareness of God's affectionate care; the mission is heavy yet a channel for divine light and connection with the enduring.
rows.anchor: الشعور بعظمة الود الحبيب الجليل الذي ينسم على روح الرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath's frame fits the truth it presents: Mount Sinai is where Moses was called, and the protected city is Mecca, the Sacred House; both clearly evoke religion and faith.
rows.anchor: وطور سينين هو الطور الذي نودي موسى - عليه السلام - من جانبه . والبلد الأمين هو مكة بيت الله الحرام

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One reported view takes the fig as a reference to Mount Tina near Damascus.
rows.anchor: قيل : إن التين إشارة إلى طور تينا بجوار دمشق

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view identifies the fig with the tree whose leaves Adam and his wife used to cover themselves in the Garden before descending to earthly life.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هو إشارة إلى شجرة التين التي راح آدم وزوجه يخصفان من ورقها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reported view locates the fig where it grew on the mountain where Noah's Ark came to rest.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هو منبت التين في الجبل الذي استوت عليه سفينة نوح

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One reported interpretation takes the olive as Mount Zeta in Jerusalem.
rows.anchor: وقيل في الزيتون : إنه إشارة إلى طور زيتا في بيت المقدس

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reported interpretation identifies the olive with Jerusalem itself.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هو إشارة إلى بيت المقدس نفسه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view makes the olive Noah's dove-carried branch, whose return signaled that the floodwaters had receded and the earth had grown vegetation.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هو إشارة إلى غصن الزيتون الذي عادت به الحمامة التي أطلقها نوح

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some say the fig and olive are simply the familiar foods, with no symbolism; another view takes them as symbols of the places where they grow.
rows.anchor: وقيل : بل التين والزيتون هما هذان الأكلان الذان نعرفهما بحقيقتهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an elsewhere mentions an olive tree beside Sinai and olives with palms; the fig is named only here. These references may suggest places or memories connected to faith or human origins in the Garden.
rows.anchor: وشجرة الزيتون إشير إليها في القرآن في موضع آخر بجوار الطور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qutb cannot be certain, but thinks the fig and olive most likely signal religious places or memories, or perhaps human beginnings in the Garden, fitting the sura's central truth and its framing style.
rows.anchor: إن الأقرب أن يكون ذكر التين والزيتون إشارة إلى أماكن أو ذكريات ذات علاقة بالدين والإيمان

rows.anchor: إن الأقرب أن يكون ذكر التين والزيتون إشارة إلى أماكن أو ذكريات ذات علاقة بالدين والإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After recognizing this truth, the value of faith, and the fate of those who reject its light and God's firm rope, how can a human being still deny the Judgment?
rows.anchor: فما يكذبك بالدين بعد هذه الحقيقة ? وبعد إدراك قيمة الإيمان في حياة البشرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's judgment among believers and unbelievers is just and wise; His justice and wisdom are manifest in this judgment.
rows.anchor: أليس الله بأعدل العادلين حين يحكم في أمر الخلق على هذا النحو

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A prophetic report from Abu Hurayra says that after reading Sura al-Tin through its last verse, one should answer, “Indeed, and I am among those who testify.”
rows.anchor: الحديث المرفوع عن أبي هريرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qutb says the sura's opening was the first revelation by consensus; accounts assigning that primacy elsewhere are unreliable.
rows.anchor: مطلع هذه السورة هو أول ما نزل من القرآن باتفاق . والروايات التي تذكر نزول غيرها ابتداء ليست وثيقة

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: In the report Qutb says is recorded in both Sahih collections, Aisha recounts true dreams preceding revelation, solitary worship at Hira, Gabriel's three commands to read, and the first five verses.
rows.anchor: عن عائشة - رضي الله عنها - قالت :

rows.speaker: خديجة
rows.claim: Khadija comforts the frightened Prophet, assuring him God will never disgrace him because he keeps kinship, speaks truth, bears others' burdens, hosts guests, and helps in crises.
rows.anchor: فقالت له : كلا . أبشر فوالله لا يخزيك الله أبدا

rows.speaker: ورقة بن نوفل
rows.claim: After hearing the account, Waraka identifies the angel as the same messenger sent to Moses and says the Prophet will be driven out; those bringing such a message are opposed, and he promises support.
rows.anchor: فقال ورقة : هذا الناموس الذي أنزل على موسى . ليتني فيها جذع

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن الزبير
rows.claim: Al-Tabari's report from Ibn al-Zubayr recounts the Prophet's alternate account: an angel brought written silk during sleep, recited the opening passage, and left it inscribed in his heart; later Gabriel appeared in the sky and identified himself.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن الزبير . قال :

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq also transmits a longer version of the revelation account through Wahb ibn Kaysan from Ubayd.
rows.anchor: وقد رواه ابن إسحاق مطولا عن وهب بن كيسان عن عبيد أيضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The event is immense in fact, meaning, and effect: God chose a human to receive His light, wisdom, words, and intended measure for humanity.
rows.anchor: قد تكرم - في عليائه - فالتفت إلى هذه الخليقة المسماة بالإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The event displays God's overflowing grace and mercy, given without cause beyond His generous nature; being remembered and addressed by God is an honor humans could never repay.
rows.anchor: يفيض من عطائه ورحمته بلا سبب ولا علة ، سوى أن الفيض والعطاء بعض صفاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Revelation redirected history by turning human conscience from earthly desires and standards toward heaven and divine revelation.
rows.anchor: إنها ليست الأرض وليس الهوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For twenty-three years believers experienced an immediate, direct connection with the heavenly realm, awaiting revelations that resolved their concerns and guided their steps; its distance from earthly sources was immense.
rows.anchor: فترة الثلاثة والعشرين عاما التالية ، التي استمرت فيها هذه الصلة الظاهرة المباشرة بين البشر والملأ الأعلى

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Anas reports that after the Prophet died, Abu Bakr and Umar visited Umm Ayman; she wept because revelation from heaven had ceased, and they wept with her. Qutb says Muslim recorded it.
rows.anchor: عن أنس - رضي الله عنه - قال : قال أبو بكر لعمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Revelation's effects endure: people derive values from heaven and law from revelation rather than earth or desire, and the event decisively changed human history.
rows.anchor: لقد ولد الإنسان من جديد باستمداد قيمه من السماء لا من الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The divine method became clear and established as a decisive criterion, so people now stray knowingly and deliberately rather than through ambiguity.
rows.anchor: وتبينت خطوطه ومعالمه . ( ليهلك من هلك عن بينة ويحيا من حي عن بينة )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only the opening passage dates to the first revelation; the sura's later portions refer to the Prophet's subsequent preaching, public worship, and pagan opposition, yet form a coherent ordered whole.
rows.anchor: فأما بقيتها فواضح أنها نزلت فيما بعد . فهي تشير إلى مواقف وحوادث في السيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As the Qur'an's first sura, it begins with God and directs the Prophet at the first heavenly contact and first step of his mission to read in God's name, beginning with the Creator.
rows.anchor: وتوجه الرسول [ صلى الله عليه وسلم ] أول ما توجه ، في أول لحظة من لحظات اتصاله بالملأ الأعلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human being begins as a small, simple-formed, fixed blood point clinging to the womb.
rows.anchor: من تلك النقطة الدموية الجامدة العالقة بالرحم . من ذلك المنشأ الصغير الساذج التكوين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This verse shows God's generosity as well as power: He raises a clinging clot to a human capable of learning, an immense transformation only His power and generosity make possible.
rows.anchor: فمن كرمه رفع هذا العلق إلى درجة الإنسان الذي يعلم فيتعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pen remains humanity's broadest and deepest tool for teaching; God knew its value and highlighted it at the opening of the final message, though its full significance was not yet apparent.
rows.anchor: لأن القلم كان وما يزال أوسع وأعمق أدوات التعليم أثرا في حياة الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since the Prophet could not write with a pen, Qutb argues that the verse's early emphasis on writing confirms that this Qur'an is revelation, not something the Prophet composed.
rows.anchor: هذا مع أن الرسول الذي جاء بها لم يكن كاتبا بالقلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is the source of all human learning and every discovery about existence, life, and the self; all knowledge comes from this one source.
rows.anchor: إن مصدره هو الله . منه يستمد الإنسان كل ما علم ، وكل ما يعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening revelation establishes a broad faith principle: every affair, movement, step, and deed begins in God's name, proceeds in His name, and returns to Him.
rows.anchor: كل أمر . كل حركة . كل خطوة . كل عمل . باسم الله

rows.speaker: ابن قيم الجوزية
rows.claim: Qutb cites Ibn al-Qayyim's summary that the Prophet remembered God in speech, commands, rulings, reports, praise, prayer, silence, and every circumstance.
rows.anchor: قال الإمام شمس الدين أبو عبد الله محمد بن قيم الجوزية في كتابه

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet praised God upon waking for reviving him after sleep and affirmed that resurrection returns to Him.
rows.anchor: وكان إذا استيقظ قال : الحمد لله الذي أحيانا بعد ما أماتنا

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha reports that when the Prophet awoke at night, he magnified and professed God's oneness ten times, then sought refuge from the constriction of this life and Judgment before beginning prayer.
rows.anchor: وقالت عائشة كان إذا هب من الليل كبر عشرا ، وهلّل عشرا

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha also reports his waking supplication seeking forgiveness, mercy, increased knowledge, a steadfast heart, and a gift of divine mercy.
rows.anchor: وقالت أيضا : كان إذا استيقظ من الليل قال : لا إله إلا أنت سبحانك

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report says that whoever wakes at night and remembers God, praises Him, and asks forgiveness or makes another supplication receives an answer; if he then performs ablution and prays, the prayer is accepted. Qutb cites Bukhari.
rows.anchor: وأخبر أن من استيقظ من الليل فقال

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet woke at night while staying with him, recited the closing verses of Al Imran, then prayed with praise affirming God's sovereignty, truth, revelation, resurrection, and the articles of faith.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس عنه [ صلى الله عليه وسلم ] ليلة مبيته عنده

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha reports that the Prophet sometimes began night prayer by asking the Lord of Gabriel, Michael, and Israfil to guide him to the truth in disputed matters.
rows.anchor: وقد قالت عائشة - رضي الله عنها - كان إذا قام من الليل قال

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: After finishing Witr, the Prophet ended it by saying “Subbuh, Quddus” three times, lengthening his voice on the third repetition.
rows.anchor: وكان إذا أوتر ختم وتره بعد فراغه بقوله : سبحان الله القدوس

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: On leaving home, the Prophet asked God's protection from straying or misleading, slipping, injustice, and ignorance; Qutb labels this report sound.
rows.anchor: وكان إذا خرج من بيته يقول : بسم الله توكلت على الله

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet taught that one who leaves home saying God's name, trusting Him, and acknowledging there is no power except through Him is guided, protected, and spared Satan; Qutb grades the report good.
rows.anchor: وقال [ صلى الله عليه وسلم ] من قال إذا خرج من بيته

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet left for dawn prayer asking God to place light in his heart, tongue, hearing, sight, and all directions, and to increase his light.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس عنه - ليلة مبيته عنده - : إنه خرج إلى صلاة الفجر

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: Abu Sa'id al-Khudri reports a supplication for going to prayer without pride, show, or malice, asking forgiveness and refuge from Hell; God appoints seventy thousand angels to seek forgiveness for the worshipper.
rows.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري : قال : قال رسول الله

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: When entering a mosque, the Prophet sought God's protection from Satan; Qutb reports that Satan then says the person is protected from him for the rest of the day.
rows.anchor: وذكر أبو داود عنه [ صلى الله عليه وسلم ] أنه كان إذا دخل المسجد

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet taught worshippers entering the mosque to pray for blessings on him and ask God to open mercy's doors, then on leaving to ask for His bounty; another report adds forgiveness and the doors of mercy or bounty.
rows.anchor: إذا دخل أحدكم المسجد فليصل وليسلم على النبي [ صلى الله عليه وسلم ] وليقل

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet used to remain in his prayer place after dawn until sunrise remembering God; he taught morning and evening remembrances. Qutb calls one report sound and cites Muslim for another.
rows.anchor: وكان إذا صلى الصبح جلس في مصلاه حتى تطلع الشمس يذكر الله

rows.speaker: أبو بكر الصديق
rows.claim: At Abu Bakr's request for morning, evening, and bedtime words, the Prophet taught a prayer seeking refuge from one's own evil, Satan, and causing harm to oneself or another Muslim; Qutb calls it sound.
rows.anchor: وقال له أبو بكر الصديق رضي الله عنه - مرني بكلمات أقولهن إذا أصبحت وإذا أمسيت

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: When putting on a new garment, the Prophet named it and praised God for clothing him, asking for its good and protection from its harm; Qutb calls the report sound.
rows.anchor: وكان [ صلى الله عليه وسلم ] إذا استجد ثوبا سماه باسمه عمامة أو قميصا

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: When returning home, the Prophet praised God for shelter, food, drink, and favor, and asked to be protected from the Fire.
rows.anchor: ويذكر عنه [ صلى الله عليه وسلم ] أنه كان يقول إذا انقلب إلى بيته

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: In the two Sahih collections, the Prophet's supplication upon entering the lavatory seeks refuge from impure male and female devils.
rows.anchor: وثبت عنه في الصحيحين أنه كان يقول عند دخوله الخلاء

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet said “Your forgiveness” after leaving the lavatory; another report, cited from Ibn Majah, praises God for removing harm and granting health.
rows.anchor: وكان إذا خرج من الخلاء قال :

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet put his hand in a water vessel and told the Companions to perform ablution in God's name.
rows.anchor: وثبت عنه أنه وضع يده في الإناء الذي فيه الماء ، ثم قال للصحابة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: When seeing the new moon, the Prophet asked God to bring it with security, faith, safety, and Islam; Qutb cites al-Tirmidhi grading this report good.
rows.anchor: ويذكر عنه أنه كان يقول

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet instructed diners to say God's name before eating and, if they forgot, to say it at the beginning and end; Qutb calls the report sound.
rows.anchor: وكان إذا وضع يده في الطعام قال : باسم الله . ويأمر الآكل بالتسمية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's entire life, down to its smallest details, was shaped by the divine instruction received at the first revelation and by its foundational faith conception.
rows.anchor: وهكذا كانت حياته كلها [ صلى الله عليه وسلم ] بدقائقها متأثرة بهذا التوجيه الإلهي
